_comment: Baseline for `nodus_gate --shapes`, which hunts the recurring bug shape:
a correct check that only one of several paths goes through.
Everything the scan currently finds is listed here. That IS the design. The
value of this phase is not the list below -- it is that the NEXT duplicated
question shows up as NEW against a recorded baseline, instead of surfacing as
issue #23 of the series two releases later.
Two verdicts, and the difference matters:
intentional -- the sites do not answer the same question, or they implement
a real protocol. Say WHY. This verdict silences the finding
forever, so it is the one to be stingy with.
tracked     -- a genuine duplicated decision that has not been paid off.
Name the issue if there is one, or say what would settle it.
`why` should record what was actually established, not what was assumed --
the same rule `tools/dependent_flakes.json` carries, and for the same reason:
an entry reading 'looks fine' is how a real one gets lost.
An entry that stops matching is reported as stale, so paying a debt down
prompts you to delete its line rather than leaving a lie behind.

`sites` on a species-A entry records how many implementations existed when the entry was written. A THIRD copy of an already-listed function matches the same key and would otherwise be silent -- found by probing the detector with a deliberate duplicate and watching it report 0 new. Growth is reported; bump the number only when you have decided the new copy is acceptable.

A `B=:` key is a pair of module-level constants enumerating the SAME vocabulary -- two voices that agree today and are kept in step by nothing (#685). Prefer paying it down over recording it: the fix is usually one import, and it is only this cheap while they still agree. An `intentional` verdict here needs to say why the two sets are genuinely two questions that happen to share members, not that they currently match.

A:register(vm,registry).why: The builtin-module registration protocol: 18 modules each register their own builtins into the VM's table. Eighteen implementations of one interface, not eighteen answers to one question. Verified by reading the call site in BuiltinRegistry.register_all.

A:handle_message(message).why: DAP and LSP. Two wire protocols with different message sets that happen to share a transport; 7% textually similar. The shared *transport* is a separate entry (_read_message) and is not intentional.

A:_read_message(stream).why: BYTE-IDENTICAL in dap/server.py:22 and lsp/server.py:124 -- JSON-RPC header framing, copied. Harmless today because framing is frozen by both specs, but the copy is real: a fix to one (a malformed Content-Length, say) reaches only one server.

A:_walk_stmt(stmt).why: #597. lsp/server.py's indexer and tooling/diagnostics.py both walk statements; the LSP one has no WorkflowDef/GoalDef case, so hover and go-to-definition are blind in step bodies. #401 fixed the diagnostics walker and left this one.

A:_walk_expr(expr).why: #597. Same pair; node-type coverage already differs (lsp lacks Nil/Str, diagnostics lacks ListLit).

A:_predeclare(stmts).why: #597's pair, third member -- lsp/server.py:382 and tooling/diagnostics.py:177. Not separately verified for drift; listed because the pair it belongs to has produced two issues.

A:lookup(name).why: Three symbol lookups: lsp/server.py, runtime/embedding.py, tooling/analyzer.py. The lsp/analyzer pair is the one that produced #401 and #597, so a third copy of 'what does this name resolve to' is worth paying attention to. Not yet compared in detail.

A:_to_host_value(value).why: Value marshalling, builtins/tool_module.py:127 vs runtime/embedding.py:1118, only 6% textually similar under the same name and signature. Two answers to 'how does a Nodus value cross the host boundary' is exactly the shape; whether they actually disagree is unverified.

A:_to_runtime_value(value).why: The other direction of the same boundary, same two modules, also 6% similar. See above.

A:_hash_tree(path).why: tooling/installer.py:44 vs tooling/registry_client.py:264, 95% similar -- a near-copy that has already drifted 5%. Content hashing used for integrity is a poor place for two nearly-identical answers; the 5% has not been characterised.

A:display_name(name).why: compiler/compiler.py:1224 vs vm/vm.py:2346, 56% similar. Both render a function name for an error message, so compile-time and run-time errors can name the same function differently. Not verified to differ in practice.

A:format_loc(loc).why: compiler/compiler.py:1234 vs vm/vm.py:375, 62% similar. Same concern as display_name: one question (how is a source location written) answered on both sides of the compile/run boundary.

A:_pause(vm,frame,reason).why: dap/server.py:113 (17 stmts) vs runtime/debugger.py:225 (45 stmts). The debugger and its DAP adapter both decide what pausing means; the size gap suggests the adapter knows less.

A:_json_get(host,port,path,token).why: cli/cli.py:546 vs services/server.py:1055. An HTTP client helper duplicated between the CLI and the server's own test/probe path.

A:_json_post(host,port,path,payload,toke.why: The sibling of _json_get, same two modules.

A:_parse_flags(args,flags_with_values,fl.why: cli/cli.py:192 vs testing/cli.py:196. Two flag parsers with the same signature; the test CLI accepting a flag form the real CLI rejects (or vice versa) would be invisible.

A:cleanup().why: runtime/sessions.py:75 and runtime/snapshots.py:91 -- unrelated resources with a conventional method name and no arguments. Same name, different subjects; nothing shared to keep in step.

A:resume_graph(payload).why: services/api.py:73 vs services/server.py:608, 11% similar. This is the file pair that produced #584 (two _graph_metadata copies that had drifted); a second duplicated entry point across the same two service layers is worth watching.

B:src/nodus/runtime/capability.py|src/no.why: GATED_BUILTINS vs BUILTIN_CAPABILITIES. They differ by exactly this one entry by design -- subprocess_shell_quote is string manipulation that runs nothing -- and tests/test_downstream_contracts.py pins the relationship. Documented in CLAUDE.md. This is the entry that proves the detector finds real pairs.

B:src/nodus/lsp/server.py|src/nodus/tool.why: False positive: the formatter's bin_prec assigns operator precedence and gives && and || their own tiers, so they are absent from its comparison-operator set. Different question from the LSP's type inference, which asks which operators yield BOOL.

B:src/nodus/tooling/analyzer.py|src/nodu.why: Same false positive as above, analyzer side.

B:src/nodus/lsp/server.py|src/nodus/tool.why: False positive: semver.py enumerates version-range comparators, not language operators.

B:src/nodus/tooling/analyzer.py|src/nodu.why: False positive: semver.py enumerates version-range comparators for dependency specifiers, which is not the language's operator set. The analyzer's list asks which operators yield BOOL. Two vocabularies that overlap because both contain comparison symbols.

B:src/nodus/tooling/formatter.py|src/nod.why: False positive, same reason: version-range comparators against the formatter's precedence tiers. Nothing keeps them in step and nothing should.

B:src/nodus/compiler/optimizer.py|src/no.why: Two opcode sets within the optimizer where one omits JUMP. Not triaged: it may be a deliberate distinction between unconditional and conditional branches, or the #518 shape. Reading remove_unreachable and its neighbours would settle it.

D:src/nodus/orchestration/task_graph.py:.why: Process-global graph registry. #585 gave a run's two STORES a shared relocatable root, but the in-memory registry has no per-runtime knob at all: a host can inject memory_store= and workflow_runner= and still shares this. Same family as #185/#390.
graph_id -> VM, process-global, and resume resolves through it. Same gap as _GRAPH_REGISTRY; #584 showed graph ids are more discoverable than assumed.

#596's leading suspect. A dispatcher set here sends steps down the worker path, where _effective_timeout_ms finds no scheduler.current_task and an agent handler runs unbounded. tests/test_task_graph.py already carries a comment saying this global leaks.

D:src/nodus/services/tool_runtime.py::TO.why: Host-provided built-in tools (nodus_execute, nodus_check, nodus_ast, nodus_dis), populated once by _ensure_registry. Guest tool.register() writes vm.tool_registry, which is already per-VM -- checked, because a guest-writable process-global here would be #185 exactly.

D:src/nodus/services/syscall_runtime.py:.why: Host-registered syscalls, built once. Nothing in or out of tree registers a custom syscall (CLAUDE.md), so there is no second participant to leak between today.
The one-shot build flag for SYSCALL_REGISTRY above.

D:src/nodus/services/agent_runtime.py::A.why: Process-wide telemetry for #424's abandoned handlers, published deliberately as abandoned_agent_calls() / abandoned_agent_call_count() and reset by reset_abandoned_agent_calls(). Host-facing, not guest-writable.

D:src/nodus/services/agent_runtime.py::_.why: The counter behind the same published surface.

D:src/nodus/vm/types.py::_STRUCTURAL_EQ_.why: A warn-once flag for the #545 record-equality staging. Process-wide is the point: the warning should fire once per process, not once per runtime.

D:src/nodus/builtins/subprocess_module.p.why: A signal-name lookup table populated at import and read thereafter. Flagged because it is built with .update(); it is a constant in everything but syntax.

D:src/nodus_lang_workflow/runner.py::_DE.why: The default workflow runner, deliberately shared and keyed by working directory, with reset_default_workflow_runner() to clear it and NodusRuntime(workflow_runner=...) as the per-tenant escape. Documented in CLAUDE.md.
The cwd key that decides when the runner above is rebuilt.
The auto-sweep daemon bound to the default runner. Shared with it by construction; #591 added the teardown that stops it.
The threading.Event that stops the auto-sweep daemon above. Shared with the runner and the thread by construction; there is nothing per-tenant about a stop signal for a process-wide thread.

A:_root_vm(vm).why: BYTE-IDENTICAL in builtins/http_module.py:390, test_module.py:21 and tool_module.py:129 -- the walk up the _caller_vm chain to the root VM. Established by reading all of them, not inferred from the name: the bodies are the same lines, and test_module's docstring says so outright ('Same pattern as tool_module._root_vm'). There is a FOURTH at subprocess_module.py:19, identical except that it has no docstring -- 7 statements against 8 -- and under the old whole-group veto that one short copy hid the other three (#736). `sites` is 3 because that is what the detector reports; the fourth sits below MIN_BODY_STATEMENTS and always will. This is the _caller_vm chain #691/#696 turned on, where two callers have already been bitten leaning on an unstated implication about it, so four private copies of 'which VM is the root of this call' is worth paying down. #751. Settled by one shared helper.

A:run().why: BYTE-IDENTICAL ASTs in dap/server.py:500 and lsp/server.py:759 -- the read/handle/break message loop. Compared with ast.unparse rather than by eye. Third member of the dap/lsp cluster already recorded here: _read_message is the transport and is tracked, handle_message is intentional because the message sets genuinely differ. The loop that drives them is the transport's half, not the protocol's, so it belongs with _read_message. Settled by lifting both into a shared server base.

A:_worker().why: The cross-file grouping is coincidence -- vm.py:2783 is an agent-call worker and shares nothing with the two in http_module beyond being a zero-arg thread body. But recording that as 'intentional' would bury the real finding underneath it: http_module.py:487 and :568 ARE near duplicates (40 diff lines over ~45), one chunking raw bytes and one parsing SSE, wrapped in the same stream/ready/holder scaffolding. Species A cannot report that pair on its own -- it requires two distinct FILES -- so this entry is where it stays visible. Settled by extracting the shared streaming scaffold.
